documents.title: General machine-condition response
documents.scope_notice: Role-specific training draft. Numeric limits are configured comparisons, not approved operating limits. Use the applicable equipment manual and site procedure.

Operator: Verify your assigned machine ID, exact sensor, timestamp, unit and data-quality flag. Preserve the reading ID and controller alarm text.
Record the alarm text, operating mode, recent job or tooling change and any visible symptoms from a safe observation point.
For Suspect, report the evidence to your supervisor and responsible maintenance team. Continue only as permitted by the approved site procedure.

For Critical or an immediate observed hazard, follow the equipment-specific approved safe-stop and site emergency procedure; keep clear and notify the responsible supervisor. This draft does not supply a button sequence or energy-isolation steps.
Do not bypass guards, open electrical panels, adjust limits, clear protective trips repeatedly or attempt unauthorized repair.
Record the concern in the incident with time, symptoms and what you observed. A normal follow-up reading is not permission to restart.
Restart only after the approved verification and release authorization; confirm the handover with your supervisor.
Supervisor: Verify machine/team scope, incident severity and the exact supporting readings; distinguish fresh evidence from last-known records.
Record the alarm text, operating mode, recent job or tooling change and any visible symptoms from a safe observation point.
For Suspect, identify the responsible operator and assign authorized maintenance review. For Critical, coordinate the approved safe response and escalate to the responsible plant manager.
Check for an existing open incident for the same concern before creating another; record a response owner and coverage/handover plan.
Confirm that the appropriate machine manual and approved procedure are available to the assigned technician. Do not use an app warning to authorize repair.
Review investigation notes, verification evidence and linked work-order completion before accepting resolution.
Record the required release/restart authorization. A cleared chart or resolved ticket alone does not authorize restart.
Maintenance: Review the assigned incident, reading IDs, units, controller alarms, operating mode and recent relevant history. Separate observation from a proposed cause.
Before servicing, apply the equipment/site-approved safe-stop, isolation and stored-energy verification procedure through authorized personnel; this draft supplies no isolation sequence.
Compare the event timeline with the equipment manual, controller alarms and a verified reference instrument where the approved inspection plan requires it.
Use an independent verification method only where authorized by the approved inspection plan. Record instrument/reference, time and result; do not infer failure from one sample.
Document actual findings and work performed, with parts/actions only when supported by inspection. Preserve pre- and post-action evidence.
Complete the approved verification and release process; abnormal follow-up readings or missing evidence require further review.
Update linked work orders and resolve the incident with meaningful verification notes and required authorization. The app does not release physical equipment.
Manager: Review affected machine/line scope and the responsible supervisor; distinguish current evidence from historical alerts.
For Critical, confirm a response owner, site escalation and a safe recovery plan with the supervisor and maintenance lead.
Use verified downtime coverage and production impact. Treat configured financial rates as assumptions until approved.
Ask for confirmed findings, verification evidence and required recovery authorization before accepting a return-to-service plan.
Track recurrence and agreed follow-up work; do not direct a repair or replacement solely from an app reading.
Admin: Verify machine identity, sensor/unit mapping, ingestion health and role/team routing within your authorized scope.
If readings are stale or missing, investigate the data path without reclassifying the machine as healthy. Preserve relevant timestamps and reading IDs.
Change only authorized configuration with a reason and retain the audit trail; do not silently alter thresholds to clear an alert.
Refer operating, isolation, repair and restart decisions to the responsible supervisor and authorized maintenance personnel.
Confirm that any operational SOP has real machine mapping, owner approval, manual reference and valid review dates before marking it approved.

Before servicing, apply the equipment/site-approved safe-stop, isolation and stored-energy verification procedure through authorized personnel; this draft supplies no isolation sequence.

Use the approved inspection plan to review mechanical loading, torque sensing and controller alarms. A torque-range load proxy is not a measured VFD load and shaft power is not electrical consumption; verify each independently where authorized.
Use an independent verification method only where authorized by the approved inspection plan. Record instrument/reference, time and result; do not infer failure from one sample.
Document actual findings and work performed, with parts/actions only when supported by inspection. Preserve pre- and post-action evidence.
Complete the approved verification and release process; abnormal follow-up readings or missing evidence require further review.
Update linked work orders and resolve the incident with meaningful verification notes and required authorization. The app does not release physical equipment.
Manager: Review affected machine/line scope and the responsible supervisor; distinguish current evidence from historical alerts.
For Critical, confirm a response owner, site escalation and a safe recovery plan with the supervisor and maintenance lead.
Use verified downtime coverage and production impact. Treat configured financial rates as assumptions until approved.
Ask for confirmed findings, verification evidence and required recovery authorization before accepting a return-to-service plan.
Track recurrence and agreed follow-up work; do not direct a repair or replacement solely from an app reading.
Admin: Verify machine identity, sensor/unit mapping, ingestion health and role/team routing within your authorized scope.
If readings are stale or missing, investigate the data path without reclassifying the machine as healthy. Preserve relevant timestamps and reading IDs.
Change only authorized configuration with a reason and retain the audit trail; do not silently alter thresholds to clear an alert.
Refer operating, isolation, repair and restart decisions to the responsible supervisor and authorized maintenance personnel.
Confirm that any operational SOP has real machine mapping, owner approval, manual reference and valid review dates before marking it approved.
